name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa / Visa-Exempt Entry

qualifying_event.description: Nationals of visa-exempt countries may enter Czechia (Schengen area) without a visa for short stays. Other third-country nationals require a Schengen (Type C) short-stay visa from a Czech diplomatic mission or another Schengen state's mission; the visa also covers purposes such as tourism, business, family visits, and even short-term/seasonal employment within the 90-day limit.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Valid passport; for visa applicants: proof of purpose, funds, return travel, insurance.

requirements.blocker_text: A short-term stay is a maximum of 90 days (within the standard Schengen 180-day rolling window). Applications are submitted at a Czech diplomatic mission.

evidence_required.document: Schengen (Type C) visa, if not visa-exempt

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days within any 180-day period

sources.title: ipc.gov.cz (Czech immigration/passport portal) -- Schengen Visa for a Stay Shorter than 90 Days: permitted purposes, application via diplomatic missions

notes: NEW ROUTE, first route of Czechia's initial build. Czechia has been a full Schengen member since 2007. Confirmed directly at tier-1, though the specific visa-exempt nationality list and precise 90/180-day rolling mechanics were not detailed on the page fetched in this pass (standard EU-wide Schengen rules assumed). dual_citizenship_allowed reflects Czechia's general policy (dual citizenship is permitted under the 2014 Citizenship Act), not something specific to this route.
